question.problem: Given that $f(x,y)=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}},$ find the set of values $(x,y)$ on which $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ exists.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $f(x,y)$ is defined only when 

$$
\begin{aligned}1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2} & \ge 0 \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & \le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the domain of $f$ is 

$$
{D}_{f}=\{(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 1\}.
$$

Now, we compute the partial derivative of $f(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{-2x}{2\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

The function ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ is defined only for 

$$
\begin{aligned}1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2} & >0 \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & <1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the domain of ${f}_{x}$ is

$$
{D}_{{f}_{x}}=\{(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}<1\}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $x$ exists on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{f}\cap {D}_{{f}_{x}} & =\{(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 1\}\cap \{(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}<1\} \\  & =\{(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}<1\}.\end{aligned}
$$
